answer: A protocol can gate each agent's payout behind a refundable stake and independently verified jobs. An attacker must lock capital for every Sybil identity, so the cost grows linearly with the fleet and funds stay unavailable during review; identities caught copying work lose their stake. At the ledge between admission and payout, enforce a rate limit: each delta in accepted work unlocks only a capped amount, delaying recovery of attack capital. An orchard of unrelated tasks also makes it harder to amortize fake identities through one repeated job.
